motivation.title: Motivation
motivation.berlinVotesBody: Every five years Berlin elects a new state parliament (Abgeordnetenhaus) — the body that shapes the city’s policies.
motivation.accessibilityBody: About [16% of German citizens](https://de.statista.com/statistik/daten/studie/1109703/umfrage/bevoelkerung-bezirke-nach-migrationshintergrund-berlin/) in Berlin come from immigrant families. Election programs are only published in German and can run up to 200 pages. That's a hard read even for native speakers. [Wahl-O-Mat](https://www.wahl-o-mat.de/berlin2026/app/main_app.html) helps, but it's not built to go deep.
motivation.clarityBody: Much of the 200 pages is rhetoric, hard to translate into anything concrete. We wanted tangible answers: separating commitments tied to numbers from general statements of intent.
motivation.whatWeDidBody: We compared the positions of 10 Berlin parties on key points across transport, housing, climate and energy, security, education, health, migration, the economy, and democracy — and turned their programs into one side-by-side table.
motivation.beforeYouVoteBody: The table is made with the help of AI; we recommend double-checking points that matter to you. Full translations of the main parties' programs are published on [BerlinVote.Help](https://www.berlinvote.help/).
motivation.furtherReadingIntro: You might also find the following useful:
motivation.furtherReadingBody:

aiDisclosure.title: AI Disclosure
aiDisclosure.intro: This page explains how we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools when creating content for this website, and how human editors remain responsible for what we publish.
aiDisclosure.howWeUseAiContent: We use AI tools to help draft and refine website text — for example, page copy and summaries of official party election programs. AI assists with wording, structure, and extracting comparable positions; it does not decide what we publish or how you should vote.
aiDisclosure.humanResponsibilityContent: All ideas, goals, and substantive decisions behind this website come from people working on the Berlin 2026 project. Before anything is published, content is reviewed for clarity and fit with the project’s informational purpose. Editorial responsibility for this website lies with the Berlin 2026 project.
aiDisclosure.reviewAndAccuracyContent: The party comparison table is compiled with substantial AI assistance from official party programs. We recommend double-checking points that matter to you. Full translations of the main parties’ programs are published on BerlinVote.Help. We check content for accuracy, but errors can still occur and some nuance may be missed. If you spot a mistake, please let us know.
aiDisclosure.contactContent: Questions about how we use AI or about the content on this site? Write to us at nina.harz@pm.me.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This privacy policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal information when you visit our website, in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable German data protection laws.
privacy.dataProcessedContent:
When you visit our website, our hosting provider may automatically process technical data required to deliver the site (for example IP address, browser type, and request timestamps in server logs). We do not operate our own user accounts and we do not ask you for your name or email on this site.

This technical processing is based on our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in providing a secure, functioning website.
privacy.hostingContent: This website is hosted by Vercel Inc. Server infrastructure and content delivery may involve processing outside the EU under appropriate safeguards. See [Vercel's Privacy Policy](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy) for details.
privacy.purposeOfProcessingContent:
We process technical data only to:

• Provide and maintain this website
• Detect, prevent and address technical issues
• Ensure the security and proper functioning of the site

This processing is necessary for our legitimate interests in providing the service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy.cookiesContent: This website does not use analytics or advertising cookies. The language preference may be stored in a small cookie or local storage so we can show your chosen language on return visits. You can delete cookies and site data in your browser settings at any time.
privacy.yourRightsIntro: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:
privacy.yourRightsList:
• Right of access (Art. 15 GDPR)
• Right to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR)
• Right to erasure (Art. 17 GDPR)
• Right to restrict processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
• Right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
• Right to object (Art. 21 GDPR)
• Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR)
privacy.contactInfo: If you wish to exercise any of these rights or have questions about your data, please contact us at nina.harz@pm.me.
